text:
Viktor Arvidsson came to Detroit to add scoring, and for most of November the scoring stopped. After an assist on Nov. 2 he went eight games without a point while the Red Wings lost seven of them, and coverage paired him with Alex DeBrincat as the two forwards whose cold spell dragged the team down. He broke out with a goal and two assists against Vancouver on Wednesday, in under 12 minutes.

Our numbers say the drought was mostly bad luck. His chances are good: 1.45 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, above last season's rate in Boston, and his 9 goals sit 1.5 below what those looks deserve. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile for scoring chances from in front of the net last season, carrying the puck in on 58% of his entries. Evolving-Hockey valued him at 2.1 wins above replacement, mostly at even strength.

The worry is five-on-five control: Detroit is outchanced with him on the ice (47% of expected goals). His points pace still sits below our talent range, which is the hopeful part for the Wings.
headline: Arvidsson's quiet month in Detroit
